text:
Maya: Heads-up — p99 TTFT spiked in us-west-2 around 10:12 UTC, Grafana panel here: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abc123/token-slo?orgId=1&from=now-30m :warning:
Oliver: Can you paste the PromQL you used? the dashboard link 403s for me from home VPN.
Maya: Sure, quick snippets I used for the drilldown:
```
sum by(shard,region) (rate(redwood_tokens_processed_total[1m]))
```
and for TTFT p99:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_token_generation_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,region,shard))
```
Oliver: Ah that per-shard `by(shard)` is key — global aggregates hide hot shards.
Raj: Node/GPU metrics show west2 pool hitting 92-96% GPU util and many pods with tiny batch sizes at the same time. Looks like long prompt tails are preventing batching.
Claire: Confirmed — customer-traffic trace shows a handful of 20k+ token requests that serialize KV cache hits and drop batching efficiency. Those kill tokens/sec/throughput for the whole shard.
Maya: Proposed fixes:
1) Add recording rules for `tokens_per_shard` and `ttft_p99_per_shard` to avoid expensive histogram queries in panels/alerts.
2) New alert: fire only when p99 TTFT > 600ms AND tokens_per_shard > 5k for 5m (so we don't alert on small noisy shards).
3) Dashboard tweak: add a `hot-shard` filter and a small multiples view for top-10 shards by tokens/sec.
Oliver: Sounds good. Any example alert rule YAML?
Maya: Draft alert (will refine in PR):
```yaml
- alert: HotShard_TTFT_Degradation
  expr: |
    (
      histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_token_generation_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,region,shard)) > 0.6
    ) and
    (
      sum(rate(redwood_tokens_processed_total[1m])) by (shard,region) > 5000
    )
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
    team: eng-sre
  annotations:
    summary: "p99 TTFT > 600ms for hot shard {{ $labels.shard }} in {{ $labels.region }}"
    runbook: "https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/hot-shard-ttft"
```
Raj: Two operational notes:
- Recording rules will increase series cardinality; route them to long-term Prometheus remote write and avoid high-res retention for >30d.
- We should pre-aggregate `tokens_per_shard` with `topk(50, ...)` on the dash so we don't explode panels for every shard.
Claire: Also let's emit a prometheus metric from the serving runtime that tags `batch_size` per-shard, so we can correlate small batches with these events. That should help automations that inject backlog slots.
Oliver: I'll pick up the PR for rules + alert. I can prototype `topk(10, sum by(shard) (...))` in a panel.
Maya: One more: tweak the alert to ignore regions with <10 qps baseline to reduce noise in new regions (apac-test etc). Use `unless` with a baseline query.
Maya: Example baseline filter: `sum(rate(redwood_tokens_processed_total[5m])) by (region) > 10`
Oliver: Good call. I'll add those guards.
sre-bot: CI check passed for prometheus/rules/hot-shard-recording.yaml, staging deploy queued :white_check_mark:
Claire: If staging looks good let's promote to prod after a 2h observation window. Also add an ops annotation to the alert with a recommended mitigation: scale dedicated pool or throttle the offending customer.
Maya: I'll open the PR and ping on the PR thread for reviews. Thanks all :thumbsup:
